nodes.summary: A real-valued function $\mu$ on a complete Boolean algebra $B$ is a measure in von Neumann's sense when $\mu(\bot) = 0$, $\mu(a) > 0$ for every $a \ne \bot$, and $\mu$ is countably additive: for every sequence $(a_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ of pairwise disjoint elements of $B$ (that is, $a_i \wedge a_j = \bot$ whenever $i \ne j$), the series $\sum_i \mu(a_i)$ converges and $\mu(\bigvee_i a_i) = \sum_i \mu(a_i)$.
nodes.title: Von Neumann measures on a complete Boolean algebra

nodes.summary: A complete Boolean algebra $B$ satisfies the countable chain condition (von Neumann's condition (5)) when every subset $S \subseteq B$ whose distinct elements are pairwise disjoint (that is, $a \wedge b = \bot$ for all distinct $a, b \in S$) is at most countable.
nodes.title: The countable chain condition for complete Boolean algebras

nodes.summary: A complete Boolean algebra $B$ satisfies the generalized distributivity law (von Neumann's condition (6)) when, for every double sequence $(a_{i,j})_{i, j \in \mathbb{N}}$ of elements of $B$ that is increasing in $j$ for each fixed $i$ (that is, $a_{i,0} \le a_{i,1} \le \cdots$ for every $i$),
nodes.title: Von Neumann's generalized distributivity law

nodes.summary: There is a complete Boolean algebra that satisfies the countable chain condition and the generalized distributivity law but carries no measure in von Neumann's sense; that is, von Neumann's sufficiency claim is false. This answers Problem 163 of the Scottish Book in the negative, in its stated form.
nodes.title: Von Neumann's conditions do not guarantee a measure

nodes.summary: The statement that every complete Boolean algebra satisfying the countable chain condition and the generalized distributivity law carries a measure in von Neumann's sense.
nodes.title: Von Neumann's sufficiency claim
